historical_reviews.v3_1: Each iteration is a four-state transaction: verified up/reachable, administratively down with carrier and peer loss, explicit up with address/route convergence, then recovered reachability. The flap controller must run through a path independent of the interface under test, and a finally-safe recovery must restore the exact original admin, address, route and membership state.

original_test_intent: Validate five controlled down/up transitions for every approved DPU management-LAN port, including expected loss while down and complete network recovery after each up.
original_method: Map each DPU port and peer, capture its original admin/carrier/address/route/bond/bridge state, establish independent rshim/console or alternate management control, execute exactly five bounded down/up cycles per approved port, record carrier and negative ping while down plus convergence and positive ping while up, abort on the first anomaly, and restore the initial network state in a supervised cleanup path.
manual_activity: The DPU/network owner approves each interface, peer, dependency and timing, confirms an independent recovery path and decides whether every down/up observation meets the criteria.
required_inputs: Management port/interface name and permanent MAC
Peer IP and direction of ping
Proof the test path is not the sole control path
safety_requirements: Do not flap an ambiguous or sole management path
Do not run over the interface under test without independent control
Capture and preserve original network state
Use exactly five bounded cycles and stop on first failure
Collect both down and up evidence
Do not auto-retry or continue after route/carrier failure
agent_execution_scope: Verify mapping, dependencies and independent control
Record original link/address/route state and baseline peer reachability
Execute only the approved bounded interface state transitions
Collect negative down-state and positive up-state evidence per iteration
Run supervised final-state restoration and validate health
engineer_actions: Approve target interface, peer and topology
Stop the sequence on isolation or error
Resolve intermittent loss and topology side effects

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The loop pings only after `up`, so it never proves expected failure while down; it uses unsafe SSH, unresolved variables, tail-only output and no cleanup trap. If SSH traverses MGT_NIC, the control/evidence channel can disappear mid-command.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: From an independent verified control path, run exactly five approved `ip link` down/up transactions per port, collecting full `ip -d link`, address/route and ping results in both states with a supervised finally-safe restoration to the captured baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Five iterations per approved port and the 10-minute source estimate remain, with exact ports, peer, timing and final-state restoration supplied by the owner.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record original state, then for each cycle prove up/reachable, down/unreachable, restored carrier/route, and up/reachable before advancing; terminate through an independent control plane and validate final equivalence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds negative proof, control-path separation, dependency mapping, convergence timing and guaranteed cleanup to the five source cycles.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Five successful pings after up do not show the link actually went down, and a final up state can hide transient route or bond failures in earlier cycles.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Administrative down may remove the test runner's path or affect shared bond/bridge traffic; ping validates IP reachability but not all management protocols or sustained throughput.

project_override_considerations: Approve whether every physical management port or logical interface is in scope, the exact peer and ping direction, bond/bridge/VLAN behavior, loss/convergence thresholds, an independent controller and the authoritative original-state restoration oracle.
expected_evidence: DPU/NIC/interface/MAC/peer/topology map, Script revision and owner approval
Independent control/recovery proof, tool versions and synchronized timestamps
Complete original link/address/route/bond/bridge and baseline ping state
Five per-port full down/link/ping-failure and up/convergence/ping-success timelines with exit statuses
Kernel/network error context and abort audit
Final state equivalence, stable peer health, preserved logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require five down/up reachability cycles per port. Missing interface and peer values are execution parameters, not contradictory source semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The flap behavior and acceptance directions are clear. Exact topology, independent recovery and parameters are identifiable prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Makes both halves of every flap observable and prevents a self-disconnecting SSH loop from being mistaken for controlled five-cycle validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: An `ip link set down` return value only proves the request was accepted; it does not prove carrier loss or peer isolation. Likewise, successful ping after `up` may use another bond member or route. Correlating physical/logical membership, carrier, routing and direction-specific reachability in both states is necessary to show the intended interface flapped and recovered, while an independent control path ensures cleanup remains possible.
